about: Estimated cooking times and serving sizes for site/data/restaurants/cook-at-home.json, recorded with the working that produced each number. Owner ruling 2026-08-16 (ROADMAP 36a/36c): estimate them, and label them as estimates. This file is the record, never the payload — nothing under site/ reads it (ADR 0047). Read data/estimates/README.md before changing it.

safety.rule: EVERY DURATION MAY DRIVE A TIMER, AND AN ESTIMATED ONE MUST BE MARKED AS AN ESTIMATE ON THE TIMER FACE. Owner ruling 2026-08-16 (ADR 0066, superseding ADR 0064's timer clause in part): 'Estimates drive timers too, clearly marked — every step gets a countdown; estimated ones are labelled as estimates on the timer face.' The food-safety argument was put to him first and overruled.
safety.source: MANDATORY wherever minutes is not null, and one of 'stated' / 'estimated'. It is what the timer face reads to mark a countdown as an estimate, so minutes without a source is the dangerous state: tools/recipe_estimates.py --check exits 1 on it.

phase.prep: no heat on the food — mixing, shaping, and heating an empty oven or pan
phase.cook: food is in the heat, as opposed to prep and wait; kept because a renderer may want to say what kind of step it is timing
phase.wait: chilling, rising, resting, marinating, cooling — passive

safety.ranges: A stated range takes its LOWER bound, matching stepDuration() in site/js/cook.js.
safety.limits: These are one assistant's estimates read off recipe text, not times measured by cooking the food. They must render labelled as estimates, never bare.

fields.serves: people served, our estimate unless servesSource is 'stated'
fields.yield: what the recipe makes (21 cakes, 1 flatbread) — NOT the same as serves
fields.timeTotal: minutes, elapsed start to serving; null where it cannot be built
fields.steps[].minutes: minutes this step takes; null with a reason where no number is honest

perfectly-pretty-hotcakes.name: Perfectly Pretty Hotcakes
perfectly-pretty-hotcakes.servesWorking: desc states the yield, not the serving: 10–15 hotcakes at 3 a person ⇒ about 4.
perfectly-pretty-hotcakes.timeTotalWorking: The recipe's own '~50 min'. Its steps state only 6 min between them, so the total is mostly the untimed prep and the 20 min it takes to fry 10–15 hotcakes one pan at a time.

steps.working: Stated by the recipe: "Leave to sit for 5 minutes to curdle." ⇒ 5 min. The 5 minutes is the milk curdling; nothing else happens in it.
Sifting four dry ingredients together and whisking them even: about 2 min.
3 eggs beaten with ¼ cup sugar to thick and pale is 2–3 min in a mixer, plus the melted butter.
Wet into dry, whisked from the centre until smooth: about 2 min.
A pan on medium-low reaches the water-dance point in about 4 min, plus the one sacrificial hotcake.

Stated by the recipe: "Cook each hotcake for a minute or so until bubbles form and pop, then flip and cook through until golden on both sides." ⇒ 1 min. Per hotcake, not per batch: at 10–15 hotcakes and one pan, the step itself runs about 20 min. A timer on it counts one hotcake.
Plating and pouring syrup.

booth-s-ginger-crunch.name: Booth's Ginger Crunch
booth-s-ginger-crunch.servesWorking: desc says the base is doubled from the original: a standard ginger crunch base is 125g butter and 1½ cups flour, so 250g and 3 cups is two of them — a 20×30cm slice tin at full depth, cut 4×6 ⇒ about 24 pieces.
booth-s-ginger-crunch.timeTotalWorking: NO NUMBER, DELIBERATELY. This record has no method at all — `steps` is empty. A total would be inventing the method as well as its duration. The owner has the recipe.

b-s-dope-as-brownie.name: B's Dope-As Brownie
b-s-dope-as-brownie.servesWorking: A single quantity — 100g chocolate, 100g butter, ½ cup flour — fills a 20cm cast-iron pan; cut 3×3 ⇒ about 9. Doubled in a baking pan (step 2) it is about 18.
b-s-dope-as-brownie.timeTotalWorking: The recipe's own '~22 min', which is the bake alone; melting and mixing add about 6 min in front of it.

steps.working: 100g butter with 100g chocolate melts in about 4 min over a low heat; sugar, 2 eggs and the dry ingredients stirred in take about 2 more.
Not an action and not timed — a note that toppings are optional and open-ended.
Not an action and not timed — a note about which dish to use, decided before step 0.
Stated by the recipe: "Bake at 170°C for about 22 minutes." ⇒ 22 min. The bake is the only timed part of this recipe.

chocolate-chewy-cookies.name: Chocolate Chewy Cookies
chocolate-chewy-cookies.servesWorking: 2 cups of flour with 185g of butter is a standard 24-cookie batch at ~35g of dough a ball; 2 cookies a person ⇒ about 12.
chocolate-chewy-cookies.timeTotalWorking: The recipe's own '15 min', which is one tray's bake. Mixing and rolling add about 12 min, and a 24-cookie batch is two or three trays.

steps.working: A melted-butter dough comes together in about 4 min; 2 cups of flour and 185g of butter make roughly 24 balls at ~20 s each, so about 8 min rolling.
Stated by the recipe: "Bake for 15 minutes at 170°C." ⇒ 15 min. One tray. A second tray repeats the 15 min.

gingerbread-cookies.name: Gingerbread Cookies
gingerbread-cookies.servesWorking: 5 cups of flour (≈750g) with 250g butter, 2 eggs and 1 cup of syrup makes about 1.7 kg of dough; at ~35g a cookie rolled to 4–5mm that is roughly 45–50 cookies, 2–3 a person ⇒ about 20. Weak: the cutter size is not stated and it changes the count outright.
gingerbread-cookies.timeTotalWorking: 10 min of mixing + 30 min chilling + 15 min rolling and cutting + 5 min chilling + 8 min a tray, and a batch this size is four or five trays baked in sequence ⇒ about 75 min elapsed.

steps.working: 250g butter creamed with 1 cup brown sugar: 3–4 min in a mixer.
Three ground spices in and mixed.
2 eggs and 1 cup of golden syrup beaten in.
5 cups of flour added slowly, in three or four goes.
Stated by the recipe: "Chill in cling film for 30 minutes." ⇒ 30 min. Chilling in cling film; the dough is unworkable warm.
About 1.7 kg of dough (250g butter, 5 cups flour, 1 cup syrup) rolled to 4–5mm and cut in batches: about 15 min.
Stated by the recipe: "Chill in the fridge for 5–10 minutes." ⇒ 5 min. A range, so the lower bound: back to the fridge for 5 min before baking.
Stated by the recipe: "Bake on the pizza setting for 8 minutes at 180°C." ⇒ 8 min. Per tray. A 1.7 kg batch is four or five trays, so the oven time repeats.

li-ge-waffles.name: Liège Waffles
li-ge-waffles.servesWorking: The record already says serves 12, and step 3 divides the dough into 12 portions — one waffle a person.
li-ge-waffles.timeTotalWorking: 15 min sponge + 60 min rise + about 8 hr overnight + 15 min shaping + 20 min at the iron ⇒ roughly 9 hr 50 elapsed, of which only about 50 min is hands-on. The overnight is our figure, not the recipe's.

steps.working: Stated by the recipe: "Let rest for about 15 minutes." ⇒ 15 min. The 15 min is the yeast sponge resting; mixing it beforehand adds 2–3 min.
Stated by the recipe: "Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour." ⇒ 60 min. The full dough rising in a warm place.
The recipe says 'overnight' and gives no hours, so this number is ours, not the recipe's: 8 hr is taken as overnight. Nothing here should ever run a timer.
12 portions shaped and rolled in pearled sugar at about 1 min each.
12 waffles at about 3 min in the iron, two at a time: about 20 min.

orange-yoghurt-cake.name: Orange Yoghurt Cake
orange-yoghurt-cake.servesWorking: Step 0 states a 20cm tin; a 125g-butter, 2-cup-flour batter fills it to a standard depth and cuts 8 slices.
orange-yoghurt-cake.timeTotalWorking: The recipe's own '~1 hr' — which is the bake alone. Prep adds about 15 min, so allow 1 hr 15 elapsed.

steps.working: Greasing and lining a 20cm tin.
125g butter creamed with 1 cup caster sugar to light and fluffy is 3–4 min, plus 3 yolks one at a time.
Two alternating additions of flour, yoghurt and juice, mixed well between.
3 egg whites to soft peaks: 2–3 min.
Folded in two stages.
Stated by the recipe: "Bake at 160°C for about 1 hour." ⇒ 60 min. The bake, and the whole of the recipe's stated total.

queen-cakes.name: Queen Cakes
queen-cakes.servesWorking: The recipe states the yield, not the serving: 21 small patty cakes at 2 a person ⇒ about 10.
queen-cakes.timeTotalWorking: The recipe's own '~12 min', which is the bake alone; creaming and filling 21 tins add about 11 min in front of it.

steps.working: 125g butter and 125g sugar creamed (about 3 min), 2 eggs one at a time, 175g flour sifted in.
21 patty tins greased and filled by spoon.
Stated by the recipe: "Bake for 10–12 minutes at 200°C." ⇒ 10 min. A range, so the lower bound: 10 min, and they are watched from there.

upside-down-plum-cake.name: Upside-Down Plum Cake
upside-down-plum-cake.servesWorking: Step 1 states a 10-inch (25cm) pan; a 1⅔-cup-flour batter in a 25cm round cuts about 10 slices.
upside-down-plum-cake.timeTotalWorking: 13 min of prep and mixing + 60 min bake + 30 min cooling ⇒ about 105 min. The oven preheat (step 0) runs underneath the mixing, so it is not added.

steps.working: A domestic oven reaches 175°C in about 10–12 min. Steps 1–5 are done while it heats, so this is not added to the elapsed total.
Butter melted and swirled round a 25cm pan.
4 plums cut into 6 wedges each — 24 wedges — and laid out in one layer.
Six dry ingredients sifted together.
½ cup butter creamed with 1 cup sugar for about 3 min, then 2 eggs beaten in.

Stated by the recipe: "Alternating, add a third of the dry ingredients and a third of the milk, beating between additions, then beat for 1 minute." ⇒ 1 min. The stated minute is the final beat only; the three alternating additions before it take about 3 min more.
Stated by the recipe: "Pour the batter over the plum wedges and bake for about 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean." ⇒ 60 min. The bake, with a skewer as the real test.
Stated by the recipe: "Cool in the pan on a wire rack for 30 minutes, then invert onto a plate to serve." ⇒ 30 min. Cooling in the pan before it will turn out in one piece.

easy-pad-thai.name: Easy Pad Thai
easy-pad-thai.servesWorking: 200g of dried rice noodles is about 50g a person for a main, and 3 eggs with 1 cup of meat matches that ⇒ 4.
easy-pad-thai.timeTotalWorking: 8 min of wok work + 2 min plating, with the 15 min noodle soak run alongside the chopping ⇒ about 25 min.

steps.working: Stated by the recipe: "Soak the noodles in hot water for around 15 minutes or until soft, rinse in cold water, drain and set aside." ⇒ 15 min. Soaking in off-the-boil water — passive, and the other prep is done during it.

Stated by the recipe: "Heat the oil in a wok or large fry pan and cook the garlic and shallots for a minute, taking care not to burn." ⇒ 1 min. Stated in words rather than digits: 'for a minute'. Garlic burns after that.

Stated by the recipe: "Add the egg and allow to set for a minute, stir, then add the noodles, prawns and meat and toss to combine." ⇒ 1 min. The stated minute is the egg setting; the noodles, prawns and meat tossed in after it add about 2 min.
Three liquids in and stirred through.
Peanuts and a cup of sprouts heated through: 2–3 min, no longer or the sprouts collapse.
Garnished and plated.

famous-brade-green-chicken-curry.name: Famous Brade Green Chicken Curry
famous-brade-green-chicken-curry.servesWorking: The only quantities in the recipe are two 400ml cans of coconut — about 800ml of sauce, which serves 4 with rice. Weak: the chicken is unquantified, so this rests on the sauce alone.
famous-brade-green-chicken-curry.timeTotalWorking: 8 min browning + 5 min building the sauce + about 20 min simmering ⇒ about 35 min. The simmer is our number and the chicken's doneness, not the clock, ends it.

steps.working: Diced chicken and an onion browning in a pan: 6–8 min. Browning is colour, not doneness — the chicken is finished at step 5, not here.
Two dried herbs stirred in.
A tablespoon of paste stirred in and fried off.
Two 400ml cans in, brought back to a simmer.
Peas in.

The recipe says 'for a while' and gives no number. 20 min is what about 800ml of coconut takes to reduce to a sauce, and it is the step that cooks the chicken through — so DONENESS GOVERNS, not this number. It must never drive a timer.

jesse-s-garlic-chicken-thighs.name: Jesse's Garlic Chicken Thighs
jesse-s-garlic-chicken-thighs.servesWorking: 1 cup of stock with a 375ml can of evaporated milk makes sauce for about 4. Weak: the thighs are unquantified, so this rests on the sauce.
jesse-s-garlic-chicken-thighs.timeTotalWorking: 13 min to the browning + 10 min reducing + 3 min for the milk and soup + 15 min covered + 3 min of greens ⇒ about 45 min.

steps.working: Oil brought up to frying heat; no food in the pan yet.
6–8 crushed cloves and a thin-sliced onion sautéed.
The onion softens in 4–5 min, then the thighs are browned for 3–4. Browning is not cooking through; step 6 is.
1 cup of stock reduced by half over a moderate heat.
A sachet of soup powder in and mixed.
Evaporated milk added slowly enough not to split — the pace is the point, not the clock.
Stated by the recipe: "Reduce the heat, put the lid on and cook a further 15 minutes." ⇒ 15 min. The covered cook that finishes the chicken, and the only duration this recipe states.
The recipe says 'a few minutes'; green beans or bok choy need about 3.
Served over rice cooked alongside.

shane-s-ribs.name: Shane's Ribs
shane-s-ribs.servesWorking: ½ cup of BBQ sauce and ½ cup of Coke is enough sauce for about 1–1.5 kg of ribs ⇒ 4. Weak: the ribs are unquantified.
shane-s-ribs.timeTotalWorking: The recipe's own '8 hr (slow cooker)', which is the slow cook alone; the rub (10 min) and reducing the sauce (about 15 min) put the elapsed time nearer 8 hr 30.

steps.working: Stated by the recipe: "Mix everything (except the ribs) over medium heat for 10 minutes." ⇒ 10 min. The rub and sauce cooked out together.
Ribs and sauce into the slow cooker and turned over.
Stated by the recipe: "Cook on low for 8 hours." ⇒ 480 min. The slow cook, and the whole of the recipe's stated total.
About a cup of slow-cooker liquid reduced to a thick sauce: 10–15 min.

lamb-shanks.name: Lamb Shanks
lamb-shanks.servesWorking: One shank a person is the standard serve, and a can of tomatoes with 1½ cups of stock covers about 4 of them.
lamb-shanks.timeTotalWorking: The recipe's own '2 hr', which is the oven time; flouring, browning and boiling up the braise add about 20 min in front of it.

steps.working: Four shanks floured and browned on every side, in a pan that will only hold two at a time.
A can of tomatoes, ¼ cup vinegar, 1½ cups stock and herbs in.
About a litre of braise brought to the boil.
Shanks into an oven dish and the braise poured over.
Stated by the recipe: "Bake at 180°C for 2 hours." ⇒ 120 min. The braise, and the whole of the recipe's stated total.

slow-cooked-chicken-noodle-soup.name: Slow-Cooked Chicken Noodle Soup
slow-cooked-chicken-noodle-soup.servesWorking: 2L of stock with 6 chicken thighs, 4 potatoes and 4 carrots ⇒ about 6 bowls of roughly 330ml.
slow-cooked-chicken-noodle-soup.timeTotalWorking: NO NUMBER, DELIBERATELY. Step 0 has no duration and cannot be given one without inventing the slow-cooker setting (about 4 hr on high, 7–8 on low), so nothing can be totalled from it. The owner's own setting settles both at once.

steps.working: NO NUMBER, DELIBERATELY. The recipe says 'until tender' and never says low or high — about 4 hr on high, 7–8 on low — so choosing one would be inventing the setting as well as the time. It is also the step that cooks 6 chicken thighs, which is exactly where a made-up number stops being a disappointing dinner. The owner's own setting would settle it.
Dried noodles take 4–8 min; the packet governs, and it is not in this recipe.

mussels.name: Mussels
mussels.servesWorking: 2 cups of wine and 90g of butter is a steam for about 1–1.5 kg of mussels, which is 4 as a starter or 2 as a main. Weak: the mussels are unquantified.
mussels.timeTotalWorking: 5 min to bring the wine and butter up + the stated 5 min covered ⇒ about 10 min.

steps.working: 2 cups of wine with 6 tbsp butter and aromatics brought to a simmer: about 5 min.

Stated by the recipe: "Add the rinsed and scrubbed mussels and cook covered for 5 minutes, until the shells open." ⇒ 5 min. Stated — and the shells opening is the real test, which is why the number is safe to time.

bbq-prawns.name: BBQ Prawns
bbq-prawns.servesWorking: NO NUMBER, DELIBERATELY. Every line of this recipe is unquantified — 'Prawns', 'Olive oil', 'Garlic' — so there is nothing to divide. It scales to whatever is bought.
bbq-prawns.timeTotalWorking: The stated hour of marinating plus about 6 min on the grill ⇒ about 1 hr 5, nearly all of it waiting.

steps.working: Stated by the recipe: "Marinate the prawns in the fridge for at least an hour." ⇒ 60 min. Stated in words: 'at least an hour'. An open-ended minimum, so the lower bound is the number, and longer is the recipe's own advice.
Laying them on the grill.
Prawns take 2–3 min a side on a hot BBQ, turned once. The recipe's test is colour ('until golden brown') and colour governs — this number must not drive a timer.

sticky-date-pudding.name: Sticky Date Pudding
sticky-date-pudding.servesWorking: 185g of flour with 185g of dates is a standard single-tin sticky date ⇒ 6. The tin size is not stated, which is the weak point.
sticky-date-pudding.timeTotalWorking: 8 min softening the dates + 4 min mixing + 25 min bake + 2 min to serve ⇒ about 40 min. The sauce is made during the bake, so its 5 min is not added.

steps.working: 185g of dates simmered in 1 cup of water until soft: 5–8 min.
60g butter and 185g flour beaten into the hot dates.
Stated by the recipe: "Pour into a tin and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes." ⇒ 25 min. The bake.

Stated by the recipe: "For the sauce, place all the sauce ingredients in a pot, bring to the boil stirring, and boil for 5 minutes." ⇒ 5 min. The sauce, boiled while the pudding is in the oven — so it adds nothing to the elapsed total.
Sauce poured over.

chocolate-self-saucing-pudding.name: Chocolate Self-Saucing Pudding
chocolate-self-saucing-pudding.servesWorking: The record already says serves 6, and step 0's 1.5–2L dish agrees with it.
chocolate-self-saucing-pudding.timeTotalWorking: The recipe's own '~35 min', which is the bake alone; the batter and the boiling water add about 10 min, so allow 45 elapsed.

steps.working: A domestic oven reaches 180°C in about 10–12 min, and the dish is lined while it does. Steps 1–4 run inside this, so it adds nothing to the elapsed total.
100g butter beaten with ¾ cup sugar, an egg and vanilla.
Three dry ingredients sifted and folded in, with liquid added to a thick batter.
Spooned into the dish.
2 cups of water boiled (about 3 min in a kettle) and poured over the back of a spoon.
Stated by the recipe: "Bake at 180°C for 35 minutes, or until cooked through (try covering two-thirds of the dish with a lid)." ⇒ 35 min. The bake, and the whole of the recipe's stated total.

tiramisu.name: Tiramisu
tiramisu.servesWorking: The record already says serves 6; the 20×20cm dish and 400g of biscuits would stretch to 8 in smaller portions.
tiramisu.timeTotalWorking: The recipe's own '30 min + chill'. The active steps as written come to nearer 39 min, and the chill is 3 hr on top of whichever you take.

steps.working: A medium pot of water brought to a simmer; no food in it, so nothing is cooking yet.
6 eggs separated and the yolks weighed up with 1 cup of sugar.

Stated by the recipe: "Set the bowl over the pot and whisk continuously for about 10 minutes, until light and fluffy." "Remove and cool for 2 minutes." ⇒ 10 + 2 = 12 min. Two stated durations in one step, so both count: 10 min over the water, then 2 min cooling. cook.js would time the first leg only, which is right — the second is a fresh decision.
250g mascarpone whisked into the cooled yolks.
500ml of cream to stiff peaks is 3–4 min in a mixer, then folded in.
400g of sponge fingers is roughly 40 biscuits, dipped one at a time and laid out: about 8 min for the first layer.
Half the mascarpone spread, a second layer of biscuits dipped and laid, the rest spread and dusted.
Stated by the recipe: "Chill for at least 3 hours, ideally overnight." ⇒ 180 min. 'At least 3 hours' — the lower bound, and the recipe itself prefers overnight.

pumpkin-pie.name: Pumpkin Pie
pumpkin-pie.servesWorking: The ingredients state a 9-inch (23cm) pie crust, and a 23cm pie cuts 8.
pumpkin-pie.timeTotalWorking: 6 min of mixing + 10 min hot bake + 30 min at 175°C + about 60 min cooling to set ⇒ about 105 min. The preheat runs under the mixing.

steps.working: 220°C is a high oven; a domestic one takes about 15 min to reach it, and steps 1–3 are done while it heats.
2 cups of pumpkin with melted butter stirred through.
2 eggs beaten, then milk, sugar, salt and four spices, then the pumpkin folded in.
Stated by the recipe: "Pour into the pie shell and bake at 220°C for 10 minutes." ⇒ 10 min. The first, hot leg of the bake.
Stated by the recipe: "Reduce the heat to 175°C and bake a further 30–40 minutes, until the filling is firm." ⇒ 30 min. A range, so the lower bound: 30 min, with the filling firming as the real test.
A custard pie has to cool before it will cut; about an hour.

caramel-banana.name: Caramel Banana
caramel-banana.servesWorking: NO NUMBER, DELIBERATELY. The recipe is written to scale — 'Bananas, sliced', 'liberal amounts' of sugar — so it serves as many as there are bananas. A count here would be inventing a quantity the recipe refuses to give.
caramel-banana.timeTotalWorking: 3 min slicing while the pan heats + about 9 min to melt the sugar and soften the banana ⇒ about 12 min.

steps.working: A pan on gentle heat while two or three bananas are sliced; nothing is in the pan yet.
Butter melted, then brown sugar, which takes 3–5 min to start melting.
Stirred slowly until the sugar becomes a caramel: 3–4 min.

creamy-mushrooms.name: Creamy Mushrooms
creamy-mushrooms.servesWorking: 200g of mushrooms and 250ml of cream as a side ⇒ 4, at 50g of mushrooms each.
creamy-mushrooms.timeTotalWorking: 6 min cooking the mushrooms down + 3 min to the boil + 4 min thickening ⇒ about 13 min.

steps.working: 200g of mushrooms cook down in 5–6 min with 30g of butter.
250ml of cream up to the boil on a high heat.
The cream reduces and thickens in 3–5 min; thickness is the test.

turkish-flatbread.name: Turkish Flatbread
turkish-flatbread.servesWorking: About 2 cups of flour in one large flatbread, torn to share with a curry or mussels ⇒ 4. desc states the yield (1 flatbread), not the serving.
turkish-flatbread.timeTotalWorking: 7 min mixing + 60 min rise (the oven preheats inside it) + 6 min shaping and seeding + 17 min baking + 2 min wrapping ⇒ about 92 min.

steps.working: Flour, yeast and salt stirred together.
300–400ml of water added bit by bit and mixed to a sloppy dough.
Stated by the recipe: "Cover with a tea towel and rise in a warm place for about 1 hour." ⇒ 60 min. The rise. The oven reaches 250°C inside it, so the preheat costs nothing extra.
Hot tray out, floured, dough scraped on and pressed out — fast, because the tray is hot.
Sprayed with water and oil and seeded.

Stated by the recipe: "Bake for about 12 minutes, brush/spray again, then bake a further 5–8 minutes until golden." ⇒ 17 min. Two stated legs: 12 min, then a further 5–8 (lower bound), with a spray between them.
Wrapped in a tea towel to hold a soft crust.
